definitions.E5:
Yes. The four-year, full-time Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science is available to international applicants. It is delivered in person at UBC Vancouver and BCIT’s Burnaby Campus.

Intake-specific restrictions should be confirmed before applying. [View the program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/).

For more information, see BCIT International Students: https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/.
definitions.E2:
No. Being eligible to apply as an international applicant does **not** automatically mean you are admitted. Admission depends on meeting either the UBC or transfer-pathway requirements and receiving an admission decision from the institution.

Your academic qualifications and GPA have not been provided, so your admission eligibility cannot yet be assessed. [Review the program’s admission requirements](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/).
definitions.E1:
**I can verify:**

- This is an active, four-year joint UBC/BCIT Bachelor of Science, full-time and in person at UBC Vancouver and BCIT Burnaby.
- International applicants may apply; this does **not** guarantee admission.
- Admission uses either a UBC pathway or a transfer pathway. The stored minimum GPA is 76%, with a 70% minimum for September 2026.
- The curriculum includes UBC and BCIT courses, such as **FSCT 7320 — Introduction to Forensic Science**, **FSCT 8150 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Theory**, and **UBC BIOC 203 — Fundamentals of Biochemistry**.

**Still needed from you:** your intended admission pathway, GPA, and completed Chemistry, Biology, English/communication, and differential-calculus studies.

**Confirm with BCIT:** whether your specific credentials and courses satisfy the pathway requirements, any intake-specific restrictions, and study-permit requirements, which are not published in this program record. BCIT/UBC must also make the final admission decision.

[Program and curriculum details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)
definitions.E3: Option 1 UBC pathway: eligible for the honours specialization, with minimum GPA 76% (70% for September 2026), 8.0 credits of UBC Chemistry (CHEM 121, 111, or 141, plus CHEM 123), 3.0 credits satisfying the UBC Communication Requirement, BIOL 112, and 3.0 credits of differential calculus.
